answer: A sybil farm fails when every new identity must pay a cost that grows with the number of identities, not just once. Require each agent to hold a bond at a vertex of a trust graph, staked POA vouched for by two established neighbors, so the k-th clone costs more than the first. Make the bond withdrawable only through a narrow inlet: a slow public unbonding queue that exposes a whole cluster at once. A lone agent stands on the ledge of that queue with nothing to hide; a farm exiting a hundred clones together trips the alarm and forfeits the bonds. Continuity, not volume, is what gets paid.
